name: regex_dialect.portability
description: Cross-SDK portability of customer `regex` rule patterns. A regex rule is authored ONCE and run by TWO engines, so a construct that only one engine accepts - or that both accept and read differently - enforces in one language and is inert in the other, with nothing on the record to say so. Measured: 30 diverging verdicts across 17 construct families. Both validators must return the same ok/not-ok verdict for every pattern here; the REASON strings are deliberately not pinned, because each engine's own parser legitimately catches some of these first and reports its own reason. NOT in this fixture, and deliberately: the SEMANTIC splits with no syntactic marker - `\d` `\w` `\s` `\b` are Unicode-aware in Python and ASCII-only in JS, `$` matches before a trailing newline in Python only, and `.` matches U+000D and U+2028 in Python only. Those cannot be rejected without banning the most common constructs in the language, so they are enumerated in SECURITY.md and the parity claim is worded to exclude them. A fixture pinning them would fail today by design.
